title: A Photonic Integrated Long-distance Quantum Communication Network
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 19 June 2026;
tldr: A four-user quantum spine-leaf network over up to 540-km fiber using twin-field QKD with high secret key rate.
motivation: To demonstrate a scalable, long-distance quantum communication network that supports full connectivity between multiple users.
method: Implemented a spine-leaf network architecture using twin-field quantum key distribution (TF-QKD) at 1.25 GHz clock rate over deployed fiber.
result: Achieved secret key rate of 9.38 × 10⁻⁹ bit per pulse over 540 km, enabling full connections between any two user pairs.
conclusion: This work shows the feasibility of practical, multi-user quantum networks over long distances, advancing quantum communication infrastructure.

title: The Riemann Hypothesis Manifested In Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 01 July 2026;
tldr: The paper establishes a formal correspondence between the Riemann Hypothesis and quantum many-body dynamics, showing that the hypothesis manifests through dynamical quantum phase transitions.
motivation: To connect a deep mathematical conjecture (Riemann Hypothesis) to observable quantum phenomena, potentially offering a new pathway to test or understand the hypothesis via quantum simulations.
method: The authors construct a Riemann-based Hamiltonian and analyze its dynamics, demonstrating that the Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to the existence of a dynamical quantum phase transition in this engineered system.
result: They show that the Riemann Hypothesis manifests as a sharp change in the dynamical behavior of the quantum system, linking the zeros of the Riemann zeta function to phase transition points.
conclusion: This work provides a novel bridge between number theory and quantum thermodynamics, suggesting that quantum phase transitions can encode deep mathematical properties.

title: Learning Pure Quantum States Almost Without Regret
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper develops an online learning algorithm for pure quantum states that achieves near-optimal regret without prior knowledge of the measurement basis.
motivation: Learning unknown quantum states from measurements is fundamental to quantum information processing, but existing methods often assume knowledge of the measurement basis or suffer from high regret. The authors aim to design a practical algorithm that learns pure states efficiently in an online setting.
method: The authors propose a follow-the-regularized-leader algorithm with a novel regularizer based on the von Neumann entropy, and analyze its regret using tools from quantum information theory and online convex optimization.
result: The algorithm achieves regret scaling as O(√T log d) for T measurements of d-dimensional pure states, matching the information-theoretic lower bound up to logarithmic factors, and does not require knowledge of the measurement basis.
conclusion: The work provides a near-optimal online learning algorithm for pure quantum states, with potential applications in quantum tomography and adaptive quantum state estimation.

title: Magnon Fluctuations Find A Structure
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 30 June 2026;
tldr: Observation of magnon squeezing in magnetic insulators driven into a non-equilibrium state.
motivation: To understand and control magnon fluctuations in non-equilibrium magnetic systems, which is relevant to quantum thermodynamics and information processing.
method: Experimental observation of magnon squeezing in magnetic insulators under non-equilibrium driving.
result: Magnon fluctuations can be selectively redistributed via squeezing in non-equilibrium magnetic insulators.
conclusion: This demonstrates a new mechanism for controlling quantum fluctuations in magnetic systems, with implications for quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Optimal Control For Rydberg Multi-qubit Operations
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents optimal control techniques for multi-qubit operations in Rydberg atom arrays, achieving high-fidelity gates with reduced crosstalk.
motivation: Rydberg atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but multi-qubit operations suffer from crosstalk and limited fidelity. Optimal control can mitigate these issues.
method: The authors apply optimal control theory to design pulse sequences for Rydberg multi-qubit gates, using numerical optimization to minimize errors and crosstalk.
result: They demonstrate significant improvements in gate fidelity and reduction of crosstalk compared to standard methods, enabling scalable multi-qubit operations.
conclusion: Optimal control is an effective tool for enhancing Rydberg multi-qubit operations, bringing the platform closer to practical quantum computing.

title: Exchange-mediated Spin–electric Control Of Single Molecules On Surfaces
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 29 June 2026;
tldr: Exchange interactions enable electric control of single-molecule spins on surfaces, demonstrated for two molecular species.
motivation: Single molecules with isolated spins are promising for quantum technologies, but controlling them electrically is challenging; exchange interactions offer a new mechanism.
method: The authors use scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy to probe and manipulate spin states of individual molecules on a surface, leveraging exchange coupling between the molecule and the substrate or between molecules.
result: They demonstrate that exchange interactions allow electric-field control of the spin state, achieving coherent manipulation and readout.
conclusion: Exchange-mediated spin-electric control provides a versatile tool for quantum control of molecular spins, advancing hybrid quantum systems.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution With A Leakage From Digital-to-analog Conversion
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: This paper analyzes security of continuous-variable QKD under information leakage from digital-to-analog conversion.
motivation: Practical CV-QKD systems may have side-channel leakage from imperfect DACs, which could compromise security if not accounted for.
method: The authors model the DAC leakage as an additional quantum channel and derive security bounds using composable security framework.
result: They show that DAC leakage can significantly reduce secret key rate and propose countermeasures to mitigate the leakage.
conclusion: DAC leakage is a realistic threat to CV-QKD security that must be addressed in practical implementations.

title: Design And Optimization Of Adaptive Diversity Schemes In Quantum Mimo Channels
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 24 June 2026;
tldr: This paper designs and optimizes adaptive diversity schemes for quantum MIMO channels to improve communication reliability.
motivation: Quantum MIMO channels suffer from fading and noise; adaptive diversity can enhance performance.
method: The authors propose adaptive diversity schemes that adjust transmission parameters based on channel conditions, and optimize them using information-theoretic metrics.
result: The optimized schemes show significant improvement in channel capacity and error rates compared to non-adaptive approaches.
conclusion: Adaptive diversity is a promising technique for practical quantum communication systems.

title: A Framework Of Partial Error Correction For Intermediate-scale Quantum Computers
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 01 July 2026;
tldr: Proposes a framework for partial error correction tailored to intermediate-scale quantum computers, balancing error suppression and resource overhead.
motivation: Full quantum error correction is too resource-intensive for near-term devices; partial error correction can improve fidelity with manageable overhead.
method: Develops a theoretical framework that allows selective correction of certain error types or subsystems, using a combination of stabilizer codes and post-selection.
result: Demonstrates that partial error correction can significantly outperform no correction and sometimes approach full correction performance for specific noise models.
conclusion: Partial error correction offers a practical path for improving quantum computations on intermediate-scale devices before full fault tolerance is achieved.

title: Planar Fault-tolerant Logical Measurements With Low Qubit Overhead
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 30 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a method for fault-tolerant logical measurements on planar surface codes with reduced qubit overhead.
motivation: Fault-tolerant logical measurements are essential for quantum error correction, but existing methods often require high qubit overhead, limiting scalability.
method: The authors propose a planar architecture for logical measurements that uses fewer ancilla qubits and simpler connectivity, leveraging lattice surgery techniques.
result: They demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves fault tolerance with significantly lower qubit overhead compared to standard approaches, while maintaining comparable error thresholds.
conclusion: This work advances practical quantum error correction by reducing resource requirements for logical measurements, bringing fault-tolerant quantum computing closer to realization.

title: Real-space Imaging Of The Electron-pair Density Hole In Molecular Auger–Meitner Decay
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 30 June 2026;
tldr: This paper uses X-ray scattering to image the electron-pair density hole in molecular Auger–Meitner decay.
motivation: Understanding the spatial redistribution of electrons during Auger–Meitner decay is important for molecular physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Time-resolved X-ray scattering experiments and theoretical modeling are used to measure changes in electron-pair density.
result: The experiment resolves the spatial redistribution of electrons, providing direct imaging of the electron-pair density hole.
conclusion: The work advances experimental techniques for studying electronic dynamics in molecules, but has no relevance to the user's research directions.

title: An Integrated Theoretical And Numerical Approach To Understand Modern Experiments On Quantum Magnetism
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 29 June 2026;
tldr: This perspective article advocates for tighter collaboration between analytical theory, numerics, and experiments to understand quantum magnetism.
motivation: Many exciting phenomena predicted by theories of quantum magnets have yet to be observed, indicating a gap between theory and experiment.
method: The paper presents an integrated theoretical and numerical approach to bridge this gap, likely discussing specific models and simulation techniques.
result: The article argues that closer collaboration is needed but does not present new results.
conclusion: Progress in quantum magnetism requires a combined effort from theorists, numerical simulators, and experimentalists.

title: Surface d-orbital Order In An Intermetallic Compound
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 29 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports the observation of surface d-orbital order in an intermetallic compound without structural or magnetic order.
motivation: The existence of orbital order with a clear band-structure fingerprint in correlated materials has been unresolved.
method: The authors used angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and other techniques to study the electronic structure of the intermetallic compound.
result: They observed an orbital order from rare earth 5d electrons that is not accompanied by structural or magnetic order.
conclusion: This finding demonstrates a new type of orbital order in intermetallic compounds, relevant to condensed matter physics.

title: Ultrashort Light Pulses Can Transform A Semiconductor Into A Topological Insulator
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates the use of ultrashort light pulses to transiently transform a semiconductor into a topological insulator via Floquet engineering.
motivation: The ability to dynamically control material properties using light could enable new functionalities, such as creating topological phases on demand.
method: The authors used ultrafast laser pulses to drive a semiconductor into a Floquet topological phase, inducing metallic surface states within the band gap.
result: They observed light-induced metallic surface states, confirming the transient transformation of the semiconductor into a topological insulator.
conclusion: Floquet engineering with ultrashort light pulses is a viable technique for creating topological phases in semiconductors, opening avenues for ultrafast optoelectronics.

title: Radioactive Molecules As Laboratories Of Fundamental Physics
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 22 June 2026;
tldr: This Perspective discusses the use of radioactive molecules containing octupole-deformed nuclei for precision tests of fundamental physics, such as symmetry violations and new physics beyond the Standard Model.
motivation: To explore the potential of radioactive molecules as a platform for measuring fundamental symmetry violations and searching for new physics at energy scales complementary to high-energy colliders.
method: The paper reviews advances in production, trapping, and molecular quantum control of radioactive molecules, and discusses how these enable precision measurements.
result: Radioactive molecules with octupole-deformed nuclei offer enhanced sensitivity to certain symmetry-violating effects, making them promising for fundamental physics tests.
conclusion: Continued progress in molecular quantum control and trapping will enable these molecules to serve as powerful laboratories for fundamental physics.

title: Fullqubit Alchemist: Quantum Algorithm For Alchemical Free Energy Calculations
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 23 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a quantum algorithm for alchemical free energy calculations, a computational chemistry method.
motivation: Alchemical free energy calculations are important for drug discovery and materials design but are computationally expensive on classical computers.
method: The authors propose a quantum algorithm that uses a hybrid quantum-classical approach to compute free energy differences via alchemical transformations.
result: The algorithm demonstrates potential quantum advantage for certain molecular systems, though practical implementation remains challenging.
conclusion: Quantum computing may accelerate alchemical free energy calculations, but further hardware improvements are needed for real-world applications.

title: Tricky Tension
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 30 June 2026;
tldr: This paper investigates the microscopic origin of line tension in water nanodroplets on flat surfaces using simulations.
motivation: The microscopic origin of line tension in wetting phenomena is not well understood, and its sign and magnitude affect wetting behavior.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations of water nanodroplets on flat surfaces were performed to study structural transitions and their effect on line tension.
result: Structural transitions in the nanodroplets were found to affect both the sign and magnitude of line tension.
conclusion: Line tension is not a constant but depends on the droplet structure, which has implications for the equilibrium description of wetting.

title: How To Probe Lattice Dynamics Using Tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin Spectroscopy
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 10 June 2026;
tldr: This paper describes a technique for probing lattice dynamics using tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin spectroscopy.
motivation: Brillouin spectroscopy is a powerful tool for studying lattice dynamics, but standard methods are limited to determining elastic constants. The author aims to show how careful experimental design can extract more detailed information.
method: The paper explains the use of a tandem Fabry–Pérot interferometer setup to perform high-resolution Brillouin spectroscopy, enabling the measurement of phonon dispersion and damping.
result: The technique allows probing of lattice dynamics beyond elastic constants, such as phonon lifetimes and anharmonic effects.
conclusion: Tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin spectroscopy is a valuable method for detailed studies of lattice dynamics in materials.

title: Data-driven Discovery Of Dynamical Models In Biology
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reviews data-driven methods for discovering dynamical models in biology, focusing on regression, network architectures, and decomposition techniques.
motivation: Biological systems are complex and often lack first-principles models, so data-driven approaches are needed to infer dynamics from time-resolved data.
method: The authors compare regression-based methods, network-based architectures, and decomposition techniques, evaluating their strengths and limitations for extracting dynamical information.
result: The review highlights the complementarity of different approaches and provides guidance on selecting methods based on data characteristics and biological questions.
conclusion: Data-driven discovery is a powerful tool for modeling biological dynamics, but careful method selection and validation are crucial.

title: Spatiotemporal Shaping Of Broadband Helical Light Pulses At Relativistic Intensities
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates the generation of helical intensity wavepackets at relativistic intensities using spatiotemporal orbital angular momentum.
motivation: To achieve controlled spatiotemporal orbital angular momentum in high-power laser pulses for applications in laser-plasma interactions.
method: Experimental demonstration using a large-scale laser facility to shape broadband helical light pulses.
result: Peak intensities above 1.4 × 10^18 W cm−2 were achieved with controlled spatiotemporal OAM.
conclusion: The technique enables relativistic-intensity helical light pulses compatible with large-scale laser facilities.

title: Self-organized Nanoplasmonic Artificial Leaf For Hot-carrier Bioelectronic Interfaces
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 24 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a self-organized nanoplasmonic artificial leaf for hot-carrier bioelectronic interfaces, enabling optoelectronic modulation and pattern recognition.
motivation: To develop a bioelectronic interface that can efficiently convert light into electrical signals for neural modulation and sensing applications.
method: The authors fabricate a nanoplasmonic structure that acts as an artificial leaf, generating hot carriers upon light absorption, which are then used to modulate bioelectronic interfaces.
result: The device exhibits linear performance over a wide range of light intensities and enables leadless, multimodal optoelectronic modulation and pixel-less optical pattern recognition.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a novel platform for bioelectronic interfaces with potential applications in neural prosthetics and optical computing.

title: Deuterated Compounds For Organic Light-emitting Diodes
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 24 June 2026;
tldr: A review of deuterated compounds for organic light-emitting diodes, focusing on material science and device performance.
motivation: Deuteration can improve the efficiency and stability of OLEDs, but the paper is purely materials-oriented.
method: Survey of recent advances in deuterated compounds, discussing synthesis, mechanisms, and device integration.
result: Deuteration enhances device lifetime and quantum yield in some OLED systems.
conclusion: Deuterated compounds offer practical benefits for OLEDs, but the work has no quantum information or thermodynamics content.

title: Overcoming The Fill-factor Limit Of Organic Solar Cells
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 19 June 2026;
tldr: This paper addresses the fill-factor limit in organic solar cells through a guest-host design that prolongs exciton lifetime.
motivation: Organic solar cells suffer from field-dependent charge generation due to exciton/charge-transfer coupling, limiting fill factor and efficiency.
method: The authors use modeling coupled with a new guest-host design to enhance exciton lifetime and improve charge generation.
result: The approach simultaneously raises the fill factor and open-circuit voltage in organic solar cells.
conclusion: The guest-host design effectively overcomes the fill-factor limit, advancing organic photovoltaic performance.

title: Forty Years Of Atomic Force Microscopy
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: A viewpoint article reviewing the history and future of atomic force microscopy.
motivation: To celebrate 40 years of AFM and discuss its diverse applications and future developments.
method: Seven scientists provide their perspectives on using AFM and its potential evolution.
result: The article summarizes various applications of AFM in physics and beyond.
conclusion: AFM remains a versatile tool with promising future developments.

title: The Physics Of GaN-based Light-emitting Diodes
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: This review examines the physics of GaN-based LEDs, focusing on polarization fields, carrier localization, and non-radiative defects.
motivation: GaN-based LEDs are crucial for modern lighting, but their efficiency is limited by physical effects that need to be understood.
method: The paper reviews three key physical effects: polarization fields, carrier localization, and non-radiative defects, synthesizing experimental and theoretical results.
result: It provides a comprehensive overview of how these effects impact LED performance, including efficiency droop and emission wavelength.
conclusion: Understanding these physics is essential for further improving LED efficiency and design.

title: The Costs And Benefits Of Physics Research
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 09 June 2026;
tldr: This paper discusses the environmental costs and benefits of physics research, advocating for including environmental impacts in cost-benefit analysis.
motivation: To highlight the environmental footprint of physics research and argue for its consideration in funding decisions.
method: Commentary and perspective piece, likely reviewing existing literature and presenting arguments.
result: Calls for integrating environmental impact assessments into the evaluation of physics research projects.
conclusion: Physics research should account for its environmental costs alongside scientific benefits.

title: A Minimal In Vitro Assay For Cell Intercalation Highlights The Importance Of Interfacial Tension And Migratory Forces
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies cell intercalation in a minimal in vitro system, focusing on mechanical forces and interfacial tension.
motivation: Understanding the mechanisms driving cell intercalation, a key process in morphogenesis, is important for developmental biology.
method: A minimal assay with four cells was used to measure the roles of junction tension and migratory forces during intercalation.
result: Intercalation is driven by both interfacial tension and migratory forces, as demonstrated in the controlled in vitro system.
conclusion: The minimal system highlights the importance of mechanical forces in cell rearrangement, providing insights into tissue morphogenesis.

title: Temporally Super-resolved Dispersive Fourier Transformation Spectroscopy
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 29 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a temporally super-resolved dispersive Fourier transformation spectroscopy technique for single-shot measurement of non-repetitive spectra.
motivation: Conventional dispersive Fourier transformation spectroscopy has limited temporal resolution, preventing observation of ultrafast spectral dynamics.
method: The authors develop a super-resolved time-stretch spectroscopy method that sequentially measures non-repetitive spectra in a single shot.
result: Proof-of-concept experiments demonstrate the ability to resolve spectral evolution of 25-GHz electro-optic comb pulses and distinguish spectra separated by 3 ps.
conclusion: The technique enables temporally super-resolved spectroscopy for ultrafast phenomena.

title: Super-Snell Scanning Light-field Display For Ultrawide-angle High-resolution Glasses-free Three-dimensional Displays
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a scanning light-field display achieving ultrawide viewing angle and high resolution using the Snell's window effect.
motivation: Glasses-free 3D displays suffer from limited viewing angle and resolution; the authors aim to overcome these limitations.
method: They design a super-Snell scanning light-field architecture that exploits Snell's window effect to expand the viewing angle.
result: The prototype demonstrates a 150° viewing angle and nearly 480-pixel resolution.
conclusion: The proposed architecture enables glasses-free 3D displays with significantly improved performance.

title: Discovery Is Not The Opposite Of Application
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 30 June 2026;
tldr: This paper argues against framing research funding as a choice between discovery and application, using economic and evidence-based reasoning.
motivation: To correct misconceptions about the relationship between fundamental and applied research in funding decisions.
method: The author presents arguments from economics, evidence, and human perspectives to show that discovery and application are complementary.
result: The paper concludes that the dichotomy between discovery and application is false and harmful to research funding.
conclusion: Research funding should not force a choice between discovery and application; both are essential and interdependent.

title: Electrospray Ion Beam Deposition For Scanning Tunnelling Microscopy Of Complex Molecules
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: This paper describes a method for depositing complex molecules onto surfaces for scanning tunnelling microscopy.
motivation: Imaging complex molecules with STM requires gentle deposition methods to avoid fragmentation.
method: Electrospray ion beam deposition is used to land intact molecules on a surface under vacuum.
result: The technique enables STM imaging of large, fragile molecules that are difficult to deposit otherwise.
conclusion: ES-IBD is a useful tool for molecular-scale imaging but has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Loss Of Echs1 In Neural Stem And Progenitor Cells Impairs Neurogenesis Via Er Stress Activation And Lipid Metabolic Reprogramming
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 01 July 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the role of ECHS1 in neural stem cells and its impact on neurogenesis through ER stress and lipid metabolic reprogramming.
motivation: Understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying neurogenesis is crucial for brain development and potential therapies for neurological disorders.
method: The authors used conditional knockout mice to delete Echs1 in neural stem and progenitor cells and performed transcriptomic, metabolomic, and epigenetic analyses.
result: ECHS1 deficiency impairs neurogenesis by activating ER stress and rewiring lipid metabolism, leading to a histone crotonylation-dependent feedback loop.
conclusion: The study identifies a mechanistic link between mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation and brain development, suggesting tauroursodeoxycholic acid as a potential therapy.

title: Dna Hypomethylation Enables The Transcriptional Repressor SlSPL-CNR To Control Fruit Flavor Ester Biosynthesis
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 01 July 2026;
tldr: This paper studies DNA hypomethylation regulating fruit flavor ester biosynthesis in tomato, unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how DNA methylation affects flavor ester accumulation in tomato fruit.
method: Genetic and molecular biology experiments identifying SlDML2-mediated hypomethylation of the SlAAT1 promoter and binding of repressor SlSPL-CNR.
result: Hypomethylation facilitates repressor binding, forming a negative feedback loop that fine-tunes flavor ester levels.
conclusion: DNA hypomethylation can enable transcriptional repression, contrary to typical activation, controlling fruit flavor.

title: Svalbard-barents Ice Sheet Instability Enhanced Delivery Of Reactive Iron To The Ocean
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 01 July 2026;
tldr: This paper studies past ice sheet instability and its impact on reactive iron delivery to the ocean, with no connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: Understanding past ice sheet dynamics and nutrient cycles to predict future climate impacts.
method: Geochemical analysis of sediment cores from the Yermak Plateau over the past 135,000 years.
result: Episodes of ice sheet retreat and advance enhanced reactive iron delivery to the ocean.
conclusion: Modern ice sheet instability could perturb high-latitude nutrient cycles.

title: Modular Synthesis Of Trisubstituted Olefins And 1,3-dienes From Renewable Alcohols Via Ligand-enabled Nickel Catalysis
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 30 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a nickel-catalyzed method for synthesizing trisubstituted olefins and 1,3-dienes from renewable alcohols.

method: A ligand-enabled nickel catalyst system is used to achieve high selectivity in the synthesis.
result: The method produces trisubstituted olefins and dienes with high selectivity from renewable alcohols.
conclusion: This approach offers a sustainable and efficient pathway to important olefin compounds.
